claim.quote: We demonstrate that charge exchange with molecular hydrogen can occur with trapped protons, and we determine the efficiency with which the molecular hydrogen ions in the trap are detected.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal reference was not retrieved.

key_value_text.quote: We demonstrate that charge exchange with molecular hydrogen can occur with trapped protons
key_value_text.value: Charge exchange of trapped protons on molecular hydrogen demonstrated; BL1 lifetime unlikely to be significantly affected

name: Detection of molecular hydrogen in a neutron beam lifetime experiment

significance.quote: We find that the result of the beam neutron lifetime performed at NIST is unlikely to have been significantly affected by charge exchange with molecular hydrogen
significance.value: Systematic study; no sigma level (the BL1 result is "unlikely to have been significantly affected")

summary.plain: Using the BL2 apparatus, the NIST team showed that trapped decay protons can swap charge with residual hydrogen gas and measured how efficiently the resulting ions are detected. They conclude the earlier NIST beam lifetime is unlikely to have been significantly affected.
summary.technical: Measurements in the BL2 proton-trap apparatus (data July 2018 - October 2020) of the production and detection of molecular hydrogen ions via charge exchange with trapped protons and their detection efficiency; the BL1 lifetime result is unlikely to have been significantly affected.

title: Detection of molecular hydrogen in a neutron beam lifetime experiment
why_it_matters: The abstract says the influence of molecular hydrogen is of particular interest because of its ubiquitous presence in ultrahigh vacuum systems and could introduce systematic error in a beam lifetime experiment.
